tool_args.rationale: Fixing the memory time constant at either 0.25 or 0.65 and refitting the other three ODE parameters gives pilot RMSE below 0.001 in both cases. Yet the two fits differ by about 0.24 in their predicted response to an illustrative matched-endpoint history contrast at H = 0.45, well above the 0.045 tolerance. The trajectory batch directly addresses this ambiguity.

considered_alternatives.option: Confirm the coupled memory ODE now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Distinct memory time constants fit the five pilot rows nearly equally well but give materially different forecasts when the prefix changes and the endpoint stays fixed.
It costs less, but unlike the trajectory batch, it is not documented to provide the prefix data needed to resolve the memory-kernel ambiguity.
The Maxwell law predicts both signs across the input steps, whereas all observed targets are positive. The Kelvin–Voigt law has no dependence on the initial state or its history.
